remoteInspectionCommand:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$hostname = (& hostname).Trim()
$userName = (& whoami).Trim()
$tools = @(& dotnet tool list --global 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString() })
$toolsExit = $LASTEXITCODE
$cmd = Get-Command mcpserver-repl -ErrorAction Stop
$link = Get-Item -LiteralPath $cmd.Source -Force
$result = [ordered]@{ timestampUtc=(Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('o'); hostname=$hostname; user=$userName; globalTools=$tools; toolListExit=$toolsExit; commandSource=$cmd.Source; linkType=$link.LinkType; linkTarget=$link.Target; resolvedTarget=$link.ResolveLinkTarget($true).FullName }
'HV_OMARCHY_SA2EF833C6:' + ($result | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8 -Compress)

localUpdateNote.text:
# Update MEMORY.md: MCP Is the Authoritative Memory Store

Explicit user request on 2026-09-27: "Add note to MEMORY.md that memories should be stored in MCP."

Store durable memories in MCP Server through the active agent's supported plugin memory operations. Search MCP memories first for operational facts and prior decisions. Local MEMORY.md and other agent-local memory files are caches or pointers, not the authoritative store. Do not treat an empty local search as evidence that MCP has no relevant memory.

This correction followed a missed host lookup: live global MCP memory MEMORY-FACT-005 says PAYTON-OMARCHY or OMARCHY means PAYTON-DESKTOP. Local MEMORY.md did not contain that mapping. Never copy credentials into memory.
